items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Billy Taylor and I used to sit and listen to Art Tatum a lot, and we'd try to catch runs and things.

ctx.x: Anyway, while we were sitting there talking... Oh, I told him, I said, "This guy plays pretty piano, but it's kind of in a slow vein..." I didn't know to use the term (?) or whatever. But I said I didn't think he could play very fast, like a lot of things that Earl Hines does.

So while we were talking about this, on the radio in one of the afternoon programs (I wouldn't have no idea whose program it was) came this record of an old tune called "China Boy." And it turned out to be the Benny Goodman Trio. And the guy said later it was Teddy Wilson, Benny Goodman and Gene Krupa. And that really blew my mind. So for I guess the next... That was 1936. Probably for the next eight years, my whole thing was wrapped up in Teddy Wilson, with maybe little sprinkles of a run or something from Art…
